derives_from: 외래어 표기법 (문교부 고시 제85-11호, 1986-01-07; maintained by the National Institute of Korean Language), 제2장 표 1 국제 음성 기호와 한글 대조표 -- the IPA-to-Hangul correspondence table the regulation names as the basis of all its other tables and as the default for any language not separately tabulated, read off its two columns (모음 앞 | 자음 앞 또는 어말). 제1장 제1항 (the 24 modern jamo only) and 제2항 (one phoneme, one symbol) are kept as written, and 제9항 supplies the 반모음 rows. 제5항 (established forms win) is honoured by `data/respell/overrides`, which outranks this file.

deviations.rule: 제3항 -- a 받침 may only be ㄱ ㄴ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ
deviations.why: Satisfied vacuously, and that is the deviation: this table writes no 받침 at all, because `word()` in `core/respell.js` builds a syllable by concatenating the emitted text of its onset, nucleus and coda and a Hangul block cannot be assembled that way (see `note`). Every coda is therefore a following ㅡ syllable. For the obstruents that is the 대조표’s own 자음 앞 또는 어말 column -- 프 브 트 드 크 그 스 즈 -- so /est/ is 에스트 and /kat/ is 카트 as prescribed, and the ㅡ epenthesis a Korean reader would supply anyway is exactly right for a foreign cluster. It is wrong for the four sonorants the standard does write as 받침: /han/ comes out 하느 for 한, /hotel/ 호테르 for 호텔, /bæŋk/ 배응크 for 뱅크. That is the largest single defect in this table and it is not expressible away: a rule that merges a coda needs the initial, the vowel and the coda together, which is 19 x 21 x 7 table entries.

deviations.rule: 제4항 -- 파열음 are never written with 된소리
deviations.why: Relaxed, but only in an onset and only where the target’s own inventory proves an aspiration contrast (`if_inventory: "pʰ"` and its siblings), which today means Mandarin, Thai and Hindi. The Institute’s own newsletter grants that an unaspirated voiceless stop is nearer 된소리 than the aspirated series 제4항 mandates, and gives as its reason that one transcriber would have to adjudicate the aspirated/tense boundary across Greek, Turkish, Dutch, Arabic, Thai and Hindi -- a cost an inventory predicate does not pay. Korean lax stops are voiceless unaspirated word-initially and voiced between vowels, so the pair that writes an unaspirated voiceless stop in *both* positions is lax initially and tense elsewhere, which is what these rules do: 라-꼬느 for /laːkɔːn/, 마이-뻬느-라이 for /majpenraj/. The standard sets its own precedent for position-conditioned letters in the 일본어 세칙 (か行 is ㄱ word-initially and ㅋ mid-word). In a coda the block is a bare ㅡ syllable where the tense letter buys nothing and reads oddly, so 대조표 is kept there: /baːt/ is 바트, not 바뜨. 제4항 covers 파열음 only, so the ㅉ of /tɕ/ and /ts/ is inside the standard, and is what its own 중국어 표기 세칙 prints (마오쩌둥).

deviations.rule: 제4항, continued -- targets whose inventory cannot prove the contrast
deviations.why: Not relaxed, and this is a considered disagreement with `content/RESPELL-SYSTEMS.md`, which names Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Thai and Vietnamese as reading better with ㅃㄸㄲ. Thai is covered above; the other five have no aspirated series in phonemic IPA, and neither does English or German, whose /p t k/ *are* aspirated and must stay ㅍㅌㅋ. The data holds no discriminator, so the choice is between printing the standard’s answer and hard-coding four language codes in a `targets` block. We print the standard’s: /toːkjoː/ is 토-쿄 where a Korean reader expects 도쿄. If the owner wants the survey’s list, it is six rules per target in `targets` (p t k -> lax when word_initial, tense otherwise). Vietnamese needs no rule at all -- its `ipa` column is simply missing the /tʰ/ of th-, and the moment it has it these rules fire on their own.

deviations.rule: 제9항 다만 -- after a consonant, [w] is written as its own syllable (트위스트), except after [ɡ], [h] and [k] (쿼터, 펭귄)
deviations.why: Applied as written for a non-tonal target, and reversed for a tonal one (`unless_inventory: "˧"`). The clause is written for European consonant clusters; the same IPA string in Mandarin, Vietnamese and Thai is a medial glide inside one syllable, and splitting it would invent a syllable in a language whose syllable count is morphemic -- 说 /ʂwɔ/ must be 숴, not 스워. Lexical tone in the `ipa` column is the one thing in the data that tracks the difference, since the medial is a property of exactly those syllable canons.

deviations.rule: the language-specific 세칙 of 제3장 (영어, 일본어, 중국어, 프랑스어 …)
deviations.why: Not applied; only 표 1, the IPA table 제2장 names as the basis of the others and as the default for anything not tabulated. The 세칙 are indexed by the source language’s own spelling, which is the index this feature cannot have, and they contradict each other on the same IPA -- 일본어 세칙 writes か as 가/카 by position, 중국어 세칙 writes pinyin b as ㅂ and z as ㅉ. Where a 세칙 form is the one a Korean reader expects, it belongs in `data/respell/overrides`, which 제5항 (established forms win) makes authoritative over this file anyway.

deviations.rule: the 대조표 has no row for tone, length, palatalisation or gemination
deviations.why: Chao tone letters are dropped (`tone: "drop"`): the standard marks no tone, and a Korean reader cannot read them. Length is dropped -- the survey’s length table gives Hangul "none", the Seoul contrast is dead for younger speakers, and the 대조표 has no long-vowel row. Russian palatalisation (`ʲ`) is dropped rather than written 니/랴, which costs 데느 for день where the 러시아어 세칙 has 덴. Gemination is dropped, because writing it needs the ㅅ 받침 of 삿포로: /mɯkatte/ is 무-카트-테, not 무캇테.

note: Hangul is a composing script and the engine is not: `word()` in `core/respell.js` concatenates the emitted text of the onset, nucleus and coda, so no rule can put an onset and a vowel into one block. Every consonant therefore emits its own C+ㅡ block -- which is exactly the 대조표’s 자음 앞 또는 어말 column -- and the 520 entries in `syllable_fixups` are the 초성+중성 composition table that merges it with the vowel that follows: 크 + 아 -> 카. This is why /str/ comes out 스트르 + 이 -> 스트리, which is the prescribed form. Two consequences to know about. A syllable gets one fixup, so a syllable needing two merges (an onset *and* a coda glide) only gets the onset one, which is why /ɚ j w/ have their own C+glide rules. And 받침 is out of reach entirely, because merging a coda needs the initial, the vowel and the coda in one rule (19 x 21 x 7 entries). One line in the engine -- normalising the assembled syllable to NFC -- would delete all 520 entries and make 받침 expressible as conjoining jamo; see the report.
